title: 2022 HMMT February Guts Problem 16
statement: Let \(A B C\) be an acute triangle with \(A\)-excircle \(\Gamma\). Let the line through \(A\) perpendicular to \(B C\) intersect \(B C\) at \(D\) and intersect \(\Gamma\) at \(E\) and \(F\). Suppose that \(A D=D E=E F\). If the maximum value of \(\sin B\) can be expressed as \(\frac{\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}}{c}\) for positive integers \(a, b\), and \(c\), compute the minimum possible value of \(a+b+c\).

solutions.text:
First note that we can assume \(A B<A C\). Suppose \(\Gamma\) is tangent to \(B C\) at \(T\). Let \(A D=\) \(D E=E F=x\). Then, by Power of a Point, we have \(D T^{2}=D E \cdot D F=x \cdot 2 x=2 x^{2} \Longrightarrow D T=x \sqrt{2}\). Note that \(C T=s-b\), and since the length of the tangent from \(A\) to \(\Gamma\) is \(s\), we have \(s^{2}=A E \cdot A F=6 x^{2}\), so \(C T=x \sqrt{6}-b\). Since \(B C=B D+D T+T C\), we have \(B D=B C-x \sqrt{2}-(x \sqrt{6}-b)=a+b-x(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6})\). Since \(a+b=2 s-c=2 x \sqrt{6}-c\), we have \(B D=x(\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})-c\). Now, by Pythagorean Theorem, we have \(c^{2}=A B^{2}=A D^{2}+B D^{2}=x^{2}+[x(\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})-c]^{2}\). Simplifying gives \(x^{2}(9-4 \sqrt{3})=x c(2 \sqrt{6}-2 \sqrt{2})\). This yields

\[\frac{x}{c}=\frac{2 \sqrt{6}-2 \sqrt{2}}{9-4 \sqrt{3}}=\frac{6 \sqrt{2}+10 \sqrt{6}}{33}=\frac{\sqrt{72}+\sqrt{600}}{33}\]
